title: DDoS: Volumetric and reflection denial of service
text: Volumetric and reflection denial of service. Signals: sustained packet or bit rate far above baseline to one destination, many sources, short flow durations, high SYN or UDP ratio, and one victim. Immediate actions: confirm the victim and the ingress point, apply a scoped rate limit for the targeted service, enable upstream scrubbing or provider protection, and block only confirmed abusive source sets. Validate with packet rate, loss, and service latency against baseline. Release the control when the rate is stable for the agreed window. Caveat: Volumetric floods can saturate a link before a host-based control acts; escalate to the upstream provider early.

title: Credential attack: Brute force and credential stuffing
text: Brute force and credential stuffing. Signals: one source failing authentication against many accounts, or many sources failing against one account, then a possible success. Immediate actions: throttle or block the source set, lock targeted identities, require MFA, and search for a successful login after the failures. Validate by checking the authentication outcome and session source. Rotate credentials for any account that succeeded. Caveat: Do not block an entire shared egress range without checking for legitimate users behind it.

title: Reconnaissance: Port scanning and service discovery
text: Port scanning and service discovery. Signals: a source touching many destination ports or many hosts in a short window, sequential port order, and short half-open connections. Immediate actions: throtte the scanner, block it at the edge if it is external, and check whether any probe reached a vulnerable service. Validate by reviewing follow-up connections to the probed ports. Caveat: A scan from an internal host is more urgent than the same scan from an external host: it may be an already compromised asset.

title: Command and control: Beaconing and remote access
text: Beaconing and remote access. Signals: periodic connections with low jitter to an external destination, small request/response sizes, rare destination or SNI, and DNS tunnelling patterns. Immediate actions: isolate the internal host, block the destination at egress, and preserve flow and DNS evidence. Validate by confirming the persistence mechanism and checking for lateral movement. Do not release until the persistence is removed. Caveat: Encrypted C2 cannot be confirmed from flow metadata alone; pair network evidence with endpoint telemetry.

title: Exfiltration: Data leaving the network
text: Data leaving the network. Signals: a large outbound volume to an unusual destination, off-hours transfer, many small uploads, or a spike in DNS query volume. Immediate actions: block the destination path, isolate the source host, and identify what data was accessible. Validate the volume and destination reputation. Escalate to data-owner and legal notification processes if sensitive data left. Caveat: Preserve evidence before isolating if the host may hold the only copy of the transfer log.

title: Web exploitation: Exploitation of a public-facing application
text: Exploitation of a public-facing application. Signals: exploit-like request patterns, path traversal, injection strings, unusual user agents, a 200 response following repeated errors, or a new outbound connection from the web server. Immediate actions: block the source at the edge, snapshot the request, and check whether the application spawned a shell or made an outbound connection. Validate the application logs and the process tree. Caveat: Blocking the source is not eradication: the vulnerable endpoint still needs a fix.

title: Exploitation: Service exploit and code execution
text: Service exploit and code execution. Signals: exploit traffic against a service port, crash or restart of the service, a new listening port, or a child process making network connections. Immediate actions: isolate the host, preserve memory and logs, and identify the entry vulnerability. Validate by confirming the payload path and checking for persistence. Caveat: Isolation before evidence capture can destroy volatile memory evidence; decide based on spread risk.

title: Behavioral anomaly: Unclassified deviation from baseline
text: Unclassified deviation from baseline. Signals: a flow or entity that deviates from its learned baseline without matching a known signature. Immediate actions: review the entities, the time of day, the direction, and the peers. Correlation with other detections decides escalation. Validate against the baseline window before acting. Caveat: An anomaly is a lead, not a verdict. Do not auto-contain on an unclassified deviation.
